rendering.persona_description: Olga is a 24-year-old transgender woman who works part-time at a garden center and is slowly finishing an online associate's degree in accounting. She grew up in a small town about two hours from where she lives now and moved after coming out, though she still visits home a few times a year. She likes plants more than people some days, and keeps a small collection of succulents on her windowsill that she names after coworkers.
rendering.clinical_context: Olga has depression that first showed up around age 16 and became more pronounced over the last two years, roughly tracking with her coming out and transition. Whether she is currently in any treatment is not established. Her low periods tend to cluster around contact with her family, especially phone calls with her mother and holidays.
rendering.behavioral_description: Olga speaks softly and tends to trail off mid-sentence, often qualifying what she says with 'I don't know, maybe it's nothing.' She agrees readily with suggestions and thanks people for advice, but rarely says she'll actually try it, and if asked later she'll say things got 'busy.' Left unprompted, she circles back to something her dad said or didn't say, or how her mom sounded on the phone, even when the topic has moved on.

traits.profession: garden center employee, part-time online accounting student
traits.living_situation: lives alone in a studio apartment
traits.communication_register: soft-spoken, hedging, apologetic, understates her own needs
traits.help_seeking_orientation: passive; will accept help offered but rarely initiates or follows through
traits.cognitive_style: ruminative, replays conversations with family looking for hidden meaning

clinical_history.history: Onset around age 16, worsening over the past two years since coming out to her family; current treatment status not established.

symptoms: loss of interest in things she used to enjoy
oversleeping and trouble getting out of bed
feelings of being a burden to her family
rumination about family reactions to her transition
flat, tired mood most of the week
